key_insight: The paper introduces Ledger, a persistent 3D object memory that helps an embodied assistant remember where objects are, what happened to them, and how their context changes over time from egocentric video. The key idea is to move beyond short-term perception toward human-like long-term memory for later retrieval.
problem_solved: AI assistants often perceive objects only momentarily and forget them once they leave view, making it hard to answer later questions like where an item was left or what was inside a container. This paper addresses the challenge of building durable, queryable object memory from everyday first-person videos.
method: Builds a persistent 3D memory representation that stores object locations across time.
Tracks object histories and contextual cues from egocentric video to support later recall.
Integrates observations into a structured memory so the assistant can retrieve past object states and placements.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners working on embodied AI, robotics, and personal assistants because it enables more reliable long-horizon reasoning about the physical world. It also provides a practical direction for memory systems that support real-world retrieval, planning, and interaction.
visual_elements: Timeline showing daily egocentric observations accumulating into memory
3D room/map diagram with object anchors and histories
Before-vs-after comparison of fleeting perception vs persistent memory
Icons for objects, containers, recall, and context linking
paper_title: Never Look Back: Understanding Persistence in 3D Object Memory from Egocentric Videos
paper_authors: Shravan Chaudhari, William Paul, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Homanga Bharadhwaj
